newsitem.title: USA: Colorado's economy growth seen slowing.
newsitem.headline: Colorado's economy growth seen slowing.

text.p: Colorado's job growth for 1997 is expected to be 49,200, a 2.9 percent increase over 1996, according to an annual report issued on Monday by the University of Colorado at Boulder.
Job growth in 1996 is estimated at 57,400, a 3.1 percent rise over the previous year.
Professor Richard Wobbekind of the College of Business and Administration said the slower growth will be welcome in Colorado, where the recent booming economy has put a strain on infrastructure.
Unemployment is forecast at 4.1 percent in 1997, the eight consecutive year that the state's unemployement rate was below that of the United States.
But the cost of living is expected to rise 3.5 percent, higher than the nation's inflation rate. Total population is expected to rise 1.6 percent to almost 3.9 million.
